registration.rule: FULL-GAME MONEYLINE. Identical in every respect to DEC-ML-003 -- same L2 logistic regression (scikit-learn LogisticRegression, C=0.05, max_iter=3000), same feature set (logit of the worst-case de-vigged market fair probability entered directly and unscaled, plus the same twenty standardised point-in-time factor edges: eleven classic and nine Statcast), same strictly-prior feature construction, same monthly refit on the first of the month frozen for that month, same opening-month exclusion (no bet before 1 May). THE ONE CHANGE, AND ITS EXACT FORM: a PLACEMENT VETO on long prices. Selection is UNCHANGED. Every candidate at decimal >= 1.80 still enters the pool, still informs the monthly threshold bisection, and is still ranked by edge; the day's up-to-four picks are chosen exactly as in DEC-ML-003. THEN, and only then, any selected pick priced at decimal >= 3.00 (American +200 or longer) is DECLINED and its slot GOES UNUSED. It is NOT backfilled by the next candidate down, and the threshold is NOT recalibrated on a capped pool. THIS DISTINCTION IS LOAD-BEARING AND WAS MEASURED. Capping the BAND -- which recalibrates the threshold on a capped fit pool and backfills the freed slot -- returned +13.98%, BELOW the uncapped +14.97%. Declining at PLACEMENT returned +16.47% over the same months. A future implementer who 'simplifies' this into a band filter will silently revert the change to a worse rule than doing nothing.
registration.threshold: PRICE BAND (unchanged from DEC-ML-003): decimal odds >= 1.80 (American -125 or longer), NO UPPER CAP ON THE BAND. Long prices remain candidates and remain in the threshold calibration. PLACEMENT VETO (the change): a selected pick at decimal >= 3.00 (American +200 or longer) is not placed. WHY +200 AND NOT SOME OTHER NUMBER: measured on 7,766 out-of-sample candidates scored walk-forward, the model's probability error changes SIGN at +200. Disjoint buckets: +150 to +180 = -1.9 (conservative), +180 to +200 = -3.8 (most conservative on the board), +200 to +260 = +4.6 (overconfident), +260 and longer = +7.1. Below +200 the model understates and is safe; at +200 it starts inflating exactly where the market is ALREADY inflated (+3.2 and +4.8 in those two buckets), so edge = p_model - fair_wc is manufactured from the model's own error and the largest reported edges sit where the estimate is least reliable. The boundary was NOT swept for the best-performing cutoff and must not be. EDGE THRESHOLD (unchanged): set on each monthly refit by bisection on the FIT DATA ONLY so the rule would have averaged 2.0 picks per day over the fit window, capped at 4 per day, no minimum. Volume is the calibration target; profit is never used to set the threshold. DE-VIG (unchanged): the least favourable (maximum) of proportional, power and Shin.
registration.stake_rule: Flat 1 unit per PLACED pick, fixed at publication, never revised. No Kelly, no confidence scaling, no progression, no chasing, no escalating unit ladder. A vetoed pick stakes NOTHING -- the unit is not redeployed onto another game, which is the whole point of declining at placement rather than capping the band. Unit size may only change between graded samples, never inside one.
registration.sample_size: Graded over 600 bets OR 150 calendar days, WHICHEVER IS LATER, counted from this registration. The 12 picks recorded under DEC-ML-003 do NOT carry over: they were placed under a different rule and pooling them would be the retrofit this project exists to avoid. DEC-ML-003's ledger stands closed and unaltered as its own record. PRE-COMMITTED FAILURE CONDITION (unchanged): if at the gate the day-block bootstrap CI90 lower bound is below zero, the rule is declared UNPROVEN and closed -- not re-tuned, not re-banded, not extended for more data. PRE-COMMITTED REPORTING (unchanged): consensus price is the headline; best-of-six may be shown alongside but never as the headline. || KNOWN WEAKNESSES, carried forward from DEC-ML-003: (a) the rule emerged from a search over ~1,900 configurations, four of which previously looked good and reversed; (b) the 1.80 band is one out-of-sample test deep; (c) it lost in 2022; (d) it carries a LOSING win-loss record and profits only because the average price beats the breakeven; (e) historical odds provenance for 2022-2025 is a consensus archive, not a verified sharp close. || NEW WEAKNESSES SPECIFIC TO THIS REGISTRATION, filed up front so they cannot be discovered later and explained away: (f) THE VETO WAS CHOSEN AFTER SEEING WHICH PRICE BUCKET LOST. It rests on 96 vetoed bets in the full record and 64 in the 15-month test window. (g) IT REVERSES A DELIBERATE PRE-REGISTERED CHOICE. DEC-ML-003 stated 'NO UPPER CAP' with a measured rationale (a +130 ceiling destroyed the edge in 2025) and listed as weakness (e) that this contradicted the brand owner's own +130 price discipline. This change moves BACK toward the owner's prior instinct, which is precisely the direction a degrees-of-freedom error would take. (h) DRAWDOWN IS WORSE, NOT BETTER. Max drawdown at flat $100 is -$1,494 capped against -$1,287 uncapped. The episodes differ in shape (12 days against 286) but this rule must never be described as risk reduction; it deploys less capital, it is not less volatile. (i) FIVE VARIANTS WERE TESTED ON THE SAME 7,766 OUT-OF-SAMPLE ROWS (uncapped, band-cap with backfill, global recalibration, tail correction from +180, tail correction from +200). The multiple-comparison budget is spent; no further variant may be run against this data. (j) 2023 ARGUES AGAINST THE VETO (-$992 on the full-period cut); only 2024-2026 support it. || WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THIS: the veto's case is that +200 and longer holds no exploitable edge for anyone. If forward results show vetoed candidates winning at or above their de-vigged market probability over a meaningful sample, the veto is wrong and is withdrawn.

registrations.status: superseded by DEC-ML-004: long-price placement veto: the model's probability error changes sign at +200, measured on 7,766 out-of-sample candidates
registrations.rule: FULL-GAME MONEYLINE. For every side of every game with a two-sided closing moneyline, compute a win probability from an L2 logistic regression (scikit-learn LogisticRegression, C=0.05, max_iter=3000) whose features are: (1) logit of the WORST-CASE de-vigged market fair probability, entered directly and unscaled, so the factors are only ever credited with what they add to the market line; plus (2) twenty standardised point-in-time factor edges, all oriented 'our side minus theirs' - eleven classic (sp_fip, sp_whip, bp_era, bp_whip, bp_fip, bp_fatigue, off, travel, rest, is_home, park_factor) and nine Statcast (sp_xwoba, sp_barrel, sp_hardhit, sp_whiff, sp_gb, off_xwoba, off_barrel, off_hardhit, off_whiff). Features are built by ml_features.py and ml_features_statcast.py, which compute every value from games STRICTLY BEFORE the game being priced. The model is REFIT ON THE FIRST OF EVERY MONTH on all prior seasons plus the current season to date, and is frozen for that month. Bet the side where model probability minus worst-case fair probability is largest. If no game clears the threshold, publish nothing. OPENING-MONTH EXCLUSION (the change from DEC-ML-002): NO BET IS PLACED IN THE FIRST CALENDAR MONTH OF ANY SEASON. Games through 30 April are used to accumulate season-to-date rates and are never bet. Rationale, as specified before any test was run: the features are season-to-date rates shrunk toward the prior season, so in April the model is largely pricing last year's rosters and cannot see injuries, trades or draft changes. Measured: April went 46-90 for -15.08% across 2023-2026 while the remaining months returned +6.36% on the same model.
registrations.threshold: PRICE BAND: decimal odds >= 1.80 (American -125 or longer). NO UPPER CAP - the rule is explicitly permitted to bet underdogs of any length, and imposing a +130 ceiling was measured to destroy the edge (2025: -0.20% to -4.07% capped, vs +11.47% uncapped). EDGE THRESHOLD: not a fixed number. On each monthly refit the threshold is set by BISECTION ON THE FIT DATA ONLY so that the rule would have averaged 2.0 picks per day over that fit window, capped at 4 picks per day, with no minimum. Volume is the calibration target; profit is never used to set the threshold. DE-VIG: the fair probability is the LEAST FAVOURABLE (maximum) of proportional, power and Shin, on the six-book consensus. The threshold is still calibrated on the fit window only, and the fit window MAY include April games — excluding April governs which games are BET, not which are learned from. Discarding April from training would throw away information the model legitimately has.
registrations.stake_rule: Flat 1 unit per pick, fixed at publication, never revised. No Kelly, no confidence scaling, no progression, no chasing. Explicitly NO escalating unit ladder: the ladder was simulated on this project's own data and busted a $100 bankroll in July on a -4.63% strategy. Unit size may only change between graded samples, never inside one.
registrations.sample_size: Graded over 600 bets OR 150 calendar days of BETTABLE season (May onward), WHICHEVER IS LATER. No profitability claim, no marketing of a record, and no paid picks product before that gate is met. PRE-COMMITTED FAILURE CONDITION, unchanged from DEC-ML-002: if at the gate the day-block bootstrap CI90 lower bound is below zero, the rule is declared UNPROVEN and closed — not re-tuned, not re-banded, not extended for more data. PRE-COMMITTED REPORTING: consensus price is the headline; best-of-six may be shown alongside but never as the headline. || KNOWN WEAKNESSES, carried forward and updated: (a) the rule emerged from a search over ~1,900 configurations, four of which previously looked good and reversed; (b) the 1.80 band was chosen on 2024 and validated on 2025 — one out-of-sample test deep, not many; (c) THE 2012-2021 TEST IS NEGATIVE: -3.67% over 2,536 bets, CI90 [-7.49, +0.08], 2 of 9 seasons positive. This is the largest sample any version has faced and it does not support the rule. It can only run the 11 classic factors because Statcast begins in 2021, so it cannot separate 'the approach fails in that era' from 'the approach needs Statcast'; the 11-vs-20-factor gap on recent seasons (+6.36% vs +14.64%) favours the second reading, but that is an interpretation, not a finding; (d) it carries a LOSING win-loss record and profits only because the average price is around +140 against a low-40s breakeven; (e) it contradicts the brand owner's stated +130 underdog ceiling; (f) 2022-2025 odds are a consensus archive, not a verified sharp close; (g) 2026 odds come from checkbestodds screenshots, book set unknown, measured hold ~6.0% vs 4.33% consensus, CLOSING-ONLY so no CLV is possible; (h) STATCAST IS UNAVAILABLE FOR 2026, so the registered 20-factor model CANNOT CURRENTLY BE RUN LIVE. Until Statcast is ingested, any 2026 result is the reduced 11-factor version, whose CI90 still includes zero.

findings.corrects: simulated rows appearing on dates that were bet live
findings.title: The page showed bets that were never placed, on days we were betting - including one at a price the rule forbids
findings.body: Backtested picks were merged into the ledger alongside live ones so the page could show a season rather than a single row. The de-duplication only skipped a simulated pick that matched a live one exactly on date, matchup and side. That held while every live date carried one pick. It broke as soon as the two rules disagreed about a day we were actually betting. WHAT APPEARED: five simulated rows on dates from 12 August onward, among them ATH @ KC on 20 August, which was never placed, and STL @ PHI at +220 on 21 August - a price DEC-ML-004 explicitly DECLINES, because backtest.json is still generated under DEC-ML-003, whose registered threshold carried no upper cap. So the same page showed a live rule vetoing long prices and a simulated rule taking them, on the same dates. Every row carried the `simulated` flag, but a reader counting rows counts them, and a ledger that adds losses the owner never took is not a ledger. WHAT IT MOVED: the pooled season figure only, from +8.88% to +9.70% ROI - the five rows were net negative, so removing them slightly IMPROVED the number, which is the direction that makes an error easy to miss. WHAT IT DID NOT TOUCH: the live record and the gate. DEC-ML-003 stands at 13 bets and -4.27%, DEC-ML-004 at its own count, both computed from the picks table alone. No live figure ever included a simulated row. FIXED: from the first live pick onward, the record for a date is exactly what was placed that date. Nothing is merged beside it.

findings.corrects: the season ROI shown on this site, and every simulated row's unit size
findings.title: Simulated picks were published at DOUBLE their real size, and the season ROI with them
findings.body: Every backtested pick on this site rendered at twice its true stake. The backtest records profit in DOLLARS at a $100 flat stake; the exporter converted those dollars to units by dividing by 50. So a one-unit $100 loss was published as -2.000 units, and at the site's $100-per-unit display, as -$200. The registration says flat 1 unit and the page said 2. WHAT IT OVERSTATED: the season figure, which pools simulated and live rows, read +25.40% ROI on 35.554 units. The correct figures are +10.81% and 15.140 units. That number was too high, on the public page, for as long as the two stakes disagreed. WHAT IT DID NOT TOUCH: the live record, the per-registration totals and the 600-bet gate. Those are computed from price_taken and the real final scores and never passed through the faulty conversion. DEC-ML-003's 13 bets at -4.27% and DEC-ML-004's live record are unaffected, and no claim was ever permitted by the gate. HOW IT HAPPENED: export_backtest's stake was raised from $50 to $100 and the divisor in the exporter was not raised with it. Nothing errored; one page simply began describing bets twice the size of the ones the rule places. FIXED: the exporter now reads params.stake out of backtest.json rather than carrying a literal, and refuses to export at all if that field is missing instead of guessing. Raising the stake again cannot silently double the page a second time.

findings.corrects: DEC-ML-004 sample_size: 'the 12 picks recorded under DEC-ML-003'
findings.title: DEC-ML-003 placed 13 bets, not 12 — the superseding registration undercounts it by one
findings.body: DEC-ML-004's registered text states that 'the 12 picks recorded under DEC-ML-003 do NOT carry over'. The correct figure is 13. The picks table holds 13 rows with prereg_ref DEC-ML-003, placed across five dates (12, 14, 15, 16 and 17 August); all 13 settled, going 6-7 for -0.556 units, -4.27%. That is the number shown in the DEC-ML-003 block above and it has always been correct — the error is in the prose of the successor registration only, and no published total was ever computed from it. IT IS NOT BEING EDITED. Registration text in this project is never rewritten; a correction is disclosed against it instead, which is the same mechanism used for known weakness (c). Rewriting the text would leave no trace that the count was ever wrong, and a ledger whose corrections are invisible is worth less than one that never claimed to be exact. NOTHING ELSE IN THE REGISTRATION IS AFFECTED: the carry-over decision, the 600-bet gate and the 150-day gate all apply to DEC-ML-004's own bets and none of them read this number.

findings.title: The day gate was counting days with action, not calendar days
findings.body: Both registrations gate a claim on '150 calendar days, counted from this registration'. The export was instead publishing the number of distinct dates on which a bet had been placed AND graded, under the field name days_elapsed. The two quantities diverge the first time a day passes without a bet, and they had already diverged: DEC-ML-003 reported days_elapsed 5 across a window that ran 12 to 18 August, six calendar days, because 13 August drew no qualifying picks. DIRECTION OF THE ERROR: conservative. The undercount can only hold the gate shut longer than registered; it could never permit a claim early, and no figure this project has published was overstated by it. FIXED: days_elapsed is now wall-time from the registration, stopping at the successor's registration for a superseded rule. The old measurement is still published as days_with_action, because how often the rule actually finds a bet is worth knowing — it just is not what the registration gates on.

findings.title: The rule now declines bets at +200 or longer — and this was decided after seeing which prices lost
findings.body: DEC-ML-003 stated NO UPPER CAP, with a reason: a +130 ceiling was measured to destroy the edge. It also listed as a known weakness that this contradicted the brand owner's own price discipline. DEC-ML-004 now DECLINES any selected pick priced +200 or longer. That is a reversal, in the direction the owner originally preferred, reached by analysis run after the results were visible — which is precisely the shape a wishful-thinking error takes, so it is stated here rather than buried. WHAT WAS MEASURED: on 7,766 candidates scored walk-forward and never used to fit the model that scored them, the model's probability error CHANGES SIGN at +200. Below it the model understates (+150 to +180: 1.9 points low; +180 to +200: 3.8 points low). At and above it the model overstates (+200 to +260: 4.6 points high; +260 and longer: 7.1 points high) — and it overstates in the same direction the market already does, so the reported 'edge' at long prices is partly manufactured by the model's own error. That is why the biggest edges on the card kept appearing on the longest prices. WHAT WAS TRIED AND FAILED: capping the price BAND instead (which backfills the freed slot) returned LESS than no cap at all. A global recalibration of the model returned less again. A tail-only correction starting at +180 was the worst of the five. A tail-only correction starting at +200 repaired the calibration almost entirely and STILL lost to simply declining the bets — which is the strongest evidence for the rule, because it says there is no edge left in that price range for even a well-calibrated model to find. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM: it is not risk reduction. Maximum drawdown is WORSE with the veto than without it. The change rests on 96 declined bets, 2023 argues against it, and five variants were tested against the same data, so the multiple-comparison budget is spent. The 13 bets recorded under DEC-ML-003 do NOT carry over: that rule is closed, its record stands unaltered above, and DEC-ML-004 starts its 600-bet gate from zero. WHAT WOULD FALSIFY IT: if declined candidates go on to win at or above their de-vigged market probability over a meaningful forward sample, the veto is wrong and gets withdrawn.

findings.title: The 2012-2021 failure was not about missing Statcast
findings.body: Weakness (c) said the pre-2022 losses could not be separated into 'the approach fails in that era' versus 'the approach needs Statcast'. Statcast has since been backfilled to 2015 (4.5M pitches) and the question is answered: running the FULL 20-factor model on 2017-2021 returned +0.13% over 1,454 bets (CI90 -5.15% to +5.44%, margin -0.06 points). The 11-factor version scored +1.71% on the same window - marginally BETTER. Statcast did not rescue the old era. So roughly 4,000 bets before 2022 say nothing, while roughly 950 from 2023 on say a lot, and the honest reading is either that something about 2022-onward genuinely differs, or that the recent window is where the rule was searched and it is fitted to it. This is recorded rather than filed as a supersede because the RULE is unchanged; only a factual statement inside it is now answered.
